title: References to methods. Are there any?
description:
```
If there are references describing the methods in your package, please
add these in the description field of your DESCRIPTION file in the form
authors (year) <doi:...>
authors (year, ISBN:...)
or if those are not available: <https:...>
with no space after 'doi:', 'https:' and angle brackets for
auto-linking. (If you want to add a title as well please put it in
quotes: "Title")
For more details:
<https://contributor.r-project.org/cran-cookbook/description_issues.html#references>
```

title: Using ::: in the `inst/*.Rd` files.
`tools/examples.R` writing to the user's home.
description:
```
Please ensure that your functions do not write by default or in your
examples/vignettes/tests in the user's home filespace (including the
package directory and getwd()). This is not allowed by CRAN policies.
Please omit any default path in writing functions. In your
examples/vignettes/tests you can write to tempdir().
For more details:
<https://contributor.r-project.org/cran-cookbook/code_issues.html#writing-files-and-directories-to-the-home-filespace>
e.g.: tools/examples.R
```

title: `man/roxygen/meta.R` using `options()` or `par()`.
description:
```
Please always make sure to reset to user's options(), working directory
or par() after you changed it in examples and vignettes and demos. ->
man/roxygen/meta.R
e.g.:
old <- options(digits = 3)
...
options(old)
For more details:
<https://contributor.r-project.org/cran-cookbook/code_issues.html#change-of-options-graphical-parameters-and-working-directory>
```

title: `man/roxygen/meta.R` uses `.GlobalEnv`.
description:
```
Please do not modifiy the .GlobalEnv. This is not allowed by the CRAN
policies.
-> man/roxygen/meta.R
For more details:
<https://contributor.r-project.org/cran-cookbook/code_issues.html#writing-to-the-.globalenv>
```

title: Include authors in `Authors@R`?
description:
```
Please always add all authors, contributors and copyright holders in the
Authors@R field with the appropriate roles.
 From CRAN policies you agreed to:
"The ownership of copyright and intellectual property rights of all
components of the package must be clear and unambiguous (including from
the authors specification in the DESCRIPTION file). Where code is copied
(or derived) from the work of others (including from R itself), care
must be taken that any copyright/license statements are preserved and
authorship is not misrepresented.
Preferably, an ‘Authors@R’ would be used with ‘ctb’ roles for the
authors of such code. Alternatively, the ‘Author’ field should list
these authors as contributors. Where copyrights are held by an entity
other than the package authors, this should preferably be indicated via
‘cph’ roles in the ‘Authors@R’ field, or using a ‘Copyright’ field (if
necessary referring to an inst/COPYRIGHTS file)."
e.g.: 'International Business Machines Corporation and others' in
utf16.h, etc...
Please explain in the submission comments what you did about this issue.
For more details:
<https://contributor.r-project.org/cran-cookbook/description_issues.html#using-authorsr>
```

title: Better API
description:
## Class names

- [x] Rename `ts_tokens` to `ts_tree`? ~~Or `tst`?~~

## Functions to read and write

`read` and `write` is nice because they are symmetric. OTOH `parse()` might be more intuitive, but I don't like `deparse()`.
Currently we have `load` and `save`, which is OK-ish.

- [x] `ts_tree_read()`, instead of `ts_parse()`?
- [x] `ts_tree_write()`, new generic?

## Functions to work on a `ts_tree` object?

- [x] `ts_tree_sexpr` 
- [x] `ts_tree_ast`
- [x] `ts_tree_dom`
- [x] `ts_tree_query`

## Functions to select nodes

Maybe use a `ts_tree` prefix for all `ts_tree` methods? ~~Or `tst` if we go with the `tst` class name?~~

- [x] `ts_tree_select()`
- [x] `ts_tree_select_query()`, merge into `ts_tree_select()`?
- [x] `ts_tree_select_refine()`, merge into `ts_tree_select()`?

For `ts_tree_select_refine()` we can have a `refine = FALSE` argument, after the `...` in `ts_tree_select()`.

For `ts_tree_select_query()` we can use named arguments to signal a TS query:
```r
ts_tree_select(tree, query = "(number) @num")
```
We might need more arguments for this, though, e.g. the names of the captures to select, and then this gets a bit clumsy:
```r
ts_tree_select(tree, query = list("(number) @num", captures = "num"))
```

## Selection helpers

Would be good to eliminate these

- [x] `ts_tree_selector_default()`, merge into `ts_tree_select()`
- [x] `ts_tree_selector_ids()`, merge into `ts_tree_select()`
- [x] `ts_tree_deleted()`

Maybe language implementations need to call `ts_tree_selector_default()` or at least define a method for it. But the user does not need to call it. So we can keep its exported generic in ts.

As for `ts_tree_selector_ids()`, we can use the name of the argument to signal node ids:
```r
ts_tree_select(ts, ids = c(1L, 5L, 10L))
```

We could use a special value instead of `ts_tree_deleted`, e.g. `NA`. This is terrible for discoverability, though. `NULL` would be OK, but there is a JSON `null` value, and we are already using `NULL` for that. So I am not sure about this, keeping `ts_tree_deleted()` might be the best option.

## Functions to operate on selections

~~Should these have a `ts_sel_` prefix? Or a `_sel` suffix? Or a `_selected` suffix?~~

Maybe use a `ts_tree` prefix for all `ts_tree` methods?

- [x] `ts_tree_unserialize()`
- [x] `ts_tree_update()`
- [x] `ts_tree_insert()`
- [x] `ts_tree_delete()`
- [x] `ts_tree_format()`

## API in the language implementation packages (e.g. tsjsonc)

- [x] `ts_tree_read_jsonc()` (= read w/ JSON language) (or `ts_parse_json()` if we choose `parse` over `read`)
- [x] `ts_tree_write_jsonc()`? Not strictly needed, but good for discoverability.

These do not deal with `ts_tree` objects at all:

- [x] `ts_serialize_jsonc()`
- [x] `ts_unserialize_jsonc()`
